research_question: Do trained g8 QFourier models place more amplitude-weighted computation than g4 models in periodic argument regions where the Q.ANT response has high residual error?
observations: Exp014 found strong phase-dependent residual error after controlling for bfloat16.
Exp015 reduced disagreement for g4 but not g8 using a global response surrogate.
A model-level occupancy diagnostic can test whether learned phases, frequencies and amplitudes concentrate g8 computation in high-residual regions.
hypothesis: Compared with g4, trained exact-cosine g8 models will have a larger amplitude-weighted fraction of activation arguments in the highest-residual phase bins, and this exposure will be positively associated with prediction disagreement across seeds.
falsification_criterion: The hypothesis is weakened if g8 does not show greater amplitude-weighted high-error-bin exposure than g4, or if exposure does not track the observed g4/g8 disagreement difference across the pre-registered seeds.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
Occupancy is observational and cannot by itself establish that high-error-region exposure causes classification disagreement.
The diagnostic test subset is fixed to 1000 examples to bound the large activation tensor analysis.
